To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
c-Jun overexpression occurs in apoptotic cells of the cerebellum following ionizing radiation.
selective c-Jun protein overexpression is associated to ionizing radiation-induced cell death in the cerebellar cortex of the rat.
selective c-Jun expression is associated with radiation-induced apoptosis in developing rat cerebellum, as shown by in situ labeling of DNA fragmentation and c-jun immunohistochemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the involvement of c-Jun in radiation-induced apoptosis in a developing tissue, the rat cerebellum.
the involvement of c-Jun and other factors, such as Bcl-2 family proteins, c-Myc and c-Fos, in radiation-induced apoptosis.
the molecular mechanisms underlying radiation-induced apoptosis in a developing brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-Jun overexpression in the cerebellar granule cells of irradiated rats is associated with apoptosis.

selective c-Jun is a critical factor in radiation-induced apoptosis in vivo, and it may serve as a target for the prevention and/or treatment of radiation-induced cell injury and death in the developing central nervous system.
the c-Jun proto-oncogene is involved in radiation-induced apoptosis, and that it is a key factor in radiation-induced apoptosis of the developing cerebellar cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ionizing radiation-induced cell death in the cerebellar external germinal layer is associated with selective c-Jun over-expression.
the selective expression of c-Jun is associated with radiation-induced cell death in the cerebellar granular layer.
the c-jun proto-oncogene plays a key role in the induction of apoptosis in the developing rat cerebellum following ionizing radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c-Jun protein may be a good target to inhibit radiation-induced cell death in the nervous system.
c-Jun overexpression can be a useful marker to identify cells undergoing apoptosis.
selective c-Jun expression is associated with radiation-induced apoptosis in vivo, but the exact role of c-Jun in this process is still unclear.
